author: reek
body: Publishing a proposal puts a payload in the outbox, and draining takes it out again. The old body published nothing: it printed the size of an empty outbox and its head-sequence, both zero, which is an assertion that cannot fail.

author: reek
body: The measurements that carry weight here are the ones that must CHANGE. An empty repo has an empty outbox and no head; after publishing it has one payload carrying the annotation that went in; after draining it is empty again. A publish that quietly did nothing would leave before and after identical, which is exactly what the old body could not tell apart.

author: reek
body: Every measurement is taken as a VALUE at the moment it is true, and only then printed. A RepoState is threaded through `__record-set`, which stores into the record and hands back the SAME one -- so `r0`, `r1` and `r2` below are three names for one object. Building the chain first and printing afterwards reports the final state three times: the first draft of this test did exactly that, read `after-size=0`, and looked like publish-proposal doing nothing. It was the drain, already applied to the record all three names share.
